title: Atomic graph warmup and sequence-safe replay for multi-stream decoding
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: We see intermittent token misalignment and rare correctness regressions when CUDA Graphs are captured and replayed across pooled CUDA streams during high-concurrency decode workloads. Root cause (spike): a subtle coupling between capture-time kernel selection (based on observed sequence length and attention patterns) and live KV cache pointers that can diverge when the same captured graph is reused with a different logical decoding sequence.

Goal: Make graph capture and replay sequence-safe and idempotent across streams without regressing steady-state throughput or adding significant tail latency. Provide an automated warmup/capture strategy that yields deterministic replay correctness and graceful fallback when replay invariants are violated.

Constraints and non-goals: We must avoid large memory or allocation overhead on the hot path; do not change model weights or alter attention math; do not block long-running requests behind global locks. This ticket focuses on capture/warmup control, stream affinity, and safe replay; kernel-level micro-optimizations may follow in subsequent tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic token-level outputs for 99.99% of 1M decode requests in canary workloads compared to baseline reference run
Correctness regression rate <= 0.01% (token mismatch) attributable to graph replay vs non-graph path
No memory growth or leaks observed across 48-hour load test on p4d cluster
First-request extra latency after instance startup or scale-up amortized under 20ms for small models and under 35ms for long-context models with prewarm enabled
Automated fallback to non-graph decode path after 3 consecutive replay verification failures with observable telemetry and alerting
risks: Warmup sequences could increase time-to-first-byte for cold instances if not amortized at boot
Overly conservative capture boundaries may reduce batching efficiency and throughput
Edge cases with custom attention kernels (e.g., fusable rotary/ALiBi variants) may require per-architecture tuning
Rollback complexity: need safe fast-path toggle and clear instrumented metrics for on-call triage
comments: 2026-02-20: Ticket opened after customer canary showed sporadic token shifts when load increased and instance autoscaled. Initial hypothesis: stale KV pointer read during replay combined with a different kernel path chosen at capture time.

2026-02-24: Spike complete. Reproduced a deterministic repro that shows pointer aliasing when a captured graph is reused with a different logical prefill length. Spike doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/CudaGraph+Warmup+Spike

2026-03-01: Prototype implemented: 'warmup capture' that runs a short deterministic prefill to capture kernels with a capture-stamp embedded in the graph meta. Microbenchmarks show correctness failures dropped from ~0.12% to ~0.003% at 1k concurrent streams, at cost of ~2% throughput in synthetic worst-case.

2026-03-05: Code review feedback from runtime team: avoid global mutexes; implement per-stream ephemeral capture contexts and use atomic capture-stamps to validate replay. Added PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5678
2026-03-08: Added heuristic to pick warmup length based on model context and observed token distribution; smaller models use 8-token warmups, long-context models use adaptive warmup up to 32 tokens.

2026-03-10: Integration tests on p4d.8xlarge: end-to-end decode correctness tests passed; observed 18ms median extra latency on first request after scale-up with prewarm enabled. Plan: trigger prewarm during instance boot to shift cost away from user-facing latency.

2026-03-12: Tuned warmup sequence and added safe-replay watchdog that verifies KV checksums for first 3 replays; on failure, falls back to non-graph path and emits telemetry. Updated acceptance criteria and moved ticket to In Progress for Q2 rollout.
